messages:
alex: Heads-up — we're provisioning extra Dedicated GPU pools in us-west-2 and eu-west-1 for the new realtime inference clusters. Need quota increases for public IPs and ENIs. Can infra kick off AWS quota requests?

maria: Thanks, alex. Numbers? region breakdown?

alex: Rough ask: us-west-2: +800 Elastic IPs, +1200 ENIs (we're using secondary ENIs per GPU instance for address pinning). eu-west-1: +400 EIPs, +600 ENIs. Also need VPC ENI per-subnet limits lifted (we're hitting 250/az in some test subnets).

devon: Do we need more NAT gateways or IPv6 support instead to avoid EIP explosion? IPv6 could cut public EIP needs if we can use dual-stack endpoints.
alex: We evaluated IPv6 — good to do long-term, but Dedicated customers require stable public IPv4 for some integrations (partner CDNs, existing firewall rules). So short-term IPv4 is required. We'll do IPv6 work in parallel but can't rely on it for the next 6 weeks.

tara: Got it. Can you paste the exact text you want me to send to AWS support? I'll create the quota cases. Also need the account IDs for both accounts (prod-dedicated and staging).
alex: Sure — use this copy: 

"""
Hello AWS Support,

We are Redwood Inference (account 123456789012 / 210987654321). We are launching additional Dedicated GPU capacity and require quota increases to support network attachments and public endpoints. Please increase the following quotas in us-west-2 and eu-west-1: 
- Elastic IPs (VPC) to 2000 in us-west-2 and 800 in eu-west-1.
- ENIs per region to 5000 in us-west-2 and 2500 in eu-west-1.
- Subnet ENI limit per AZ to 500 per subnet where applicable.
- Increase default VPC IPv6 CIDR allocation availability so we can allocate /56s to new VPCs (requesting guidance if a larger allocation is needed).

We are on an accelerated timeline: first batch in us-west-2 needs capacity by 2026-04-10. We can provide instance IDs and fleet manifests on request. If there are alternate AWS features to achieve equivalent behavior (e.g., AWS Global Accelerator, private ips + proxying), please suggest.

Thanks,
Redwood Inference Networking
"""

tara: Copying that into the support UI now. Creating one consolidated case per region. Assigning priority as Business-critical.

infra-bot: Case created: Case #AWS-2026-4782 (us-west-2 quota increase). Estimated response within 24-48 hours.

maria: Also pinging account team/AM — if we can get an account rep to pre-approve, they'll expedite. I'll loop in claire from AWS.

devon: A couple of notes for the request body: include planned instance types (A100/p4d equivalents) and expected ephemeral ENI usage pattern (we attach 2-3 ENIs per host during warm-up). AWS sometimes asks for architecture details.

alex: Added: fleet will launch ~300 p4d-like instances initially in us-west-2 with autoscaling targeting 100% of reserved capacity, ephemeral attach/detach rate ~10/min across the fleet during scale events.

infra-bot: Case updated: Case #AWS-2026-4782 — added architecture details.

tara: Quick question — do we want a separate NAT gateway EIP pool request vs standard EIPs? Some of our infra uses EIPs for floating service IPs, others are used by NAT gateways. Separating may help AWS understand usage.

alex: Yes, separate: request 50 dedicated EIPs for NAT gateways in each region (we'll run multi-AZ NATs), rest for service floating IPs.

sre-oncall: FYI — on prior quota increases AWS asked for projected 6‑month growth. We should include a short growth table: month 0 baseline, month 1 ramp to 60%, month 3 to 90%.

maria: Added 6-month projection to the case. Also requesting ENA limit increases (network interfaces per instance family) — some instance types have lower per-instance ENIs.

infra-bot: Case created: Case #AWS-2026-4783 (eu-west-1 quota increase).

alex: Thanks — will prepare a brief internal doc for compliance to show why IPv4 sticky addresses are needed to avoid breaking customer certificates and legacy partner integrations.

tara: AWS replied, initial throughput question: they want exact CIDR usage and whether we can consolidate into fewer public IPs behind load balancers. I'll reply that certain control/control-plane endpoints must be directly addressable and cannot be behind ALBs.

maria: Claire (AWS AM) says she can fast-track if we provide a contactable architecture review; she offered a phone call tomorrow 11am PT. I'm scheduling and will invite alex, tara, and devon.

infra-bot: Update: Case #AWS-2026-4782 — AWS approved Elastic IP increase in us-west-2 to 1800 immediately; ENI approval pending follow-up.

alex: Partial win — we'll take 1800 immediately and continue pushing for full. Update fleet planning to assume 1800 EIPs in us-west-2 for the first launch.

sre-oncall: Once AWS gives final ENI numbers, we should run a quick smoke test: spin a mini fleet and validate attach/detach rates and ip allocation logic. Also check our ipam automation doesn't exceed new per-subnet limits.

tara: Closing loop: case #AWS-2026-4783 (eu-west-1) approved EIPs to 650 and ENIs to 800. Case #AWS-2026-4782 still waiting on final ENI quota.

alex: Thanks everyone. Next steps: tara to confirm final ENI numbers and post case IDs + screenshots; devon to schedule smoke test once we have final quotas; maria to run the AM call.

maria: AM call confirmed for 11am PT. Claire will try to accelerate ENI approval.

infra-bot: Thread archived by infra-bot (automated).
